newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks shun Dow advance to close flat.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks shun Dow advance to close flat.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed virtually flat after a session in which volume was thin, local investors were cautious and foreigners were conspicuously absent, traders said.

"The market was halted today by a feeling among some that stocks are overbought, continuing political uncertainty and the lack of news from the United States," said Jaime Fernandez, an analyst at brokerage Interacciones.
"They were also awaiting (Mexican) August inflation figures and waiting to see what will happen at tomorrow's primary Cetes (Treasury bill) auction," he added.
The Mexican market's blue chip IPC index closed up a scant 0.26 points, or 0.01 percent, at 3,341.19.
Brokers were surprised that Mexican stocks did not ride up on the coattails of the Dow, which rallied 73.98 points, or 1.31 percent, to close at 5,733.84.
Volume totalled just 44.7 million shares traded.
Technical analysts nonetheless were optimistic and felt the market was just passing through a consolidation period accompanied by profit-taking.

"The new short-term objective is at about 3,360 points where market consolidation should continue. It would be desirable for volume to increase, for the market to gather strength and reach new highs," said a weekly report by the Valores Finamex brokerage.

Equity investments were expected to be made more attractive by an expected fall in primary interest rates at Tuesday's auction. The key 28-day Cetes rate was expected to fall by up to 1 percentage point to around 24.5 percent, dealers said.
Hopes for a steep rate drop were bolstered by a better-than-expected 1.33 percent rise in the August consumer price index released just before the market closed on Monday.
A total of 101 stocks changed hands, of which winners outnumbered losers 42 to 37, while 22 were unchanged.
Warehousing and holding company Accelsa A2 series share prices increased 1.70 pesos ($0.23) to 12.50 pesos ($1.66), to head the winners' list and 332,000 units were traded.
"This stock is very undervalued, very cheap and some entered the market today to buy it," a dealer said.

Some brokers said that the bolsa was influenced by the dull performance of some Mexican ADRs listed in New York, where market heavyweights Telmex and Televisa both closed 1/8 down at 32-7/8 and 30-1/2, respectively.
In New York, Lehman Brothers on Monday cut its 1997 earnings estimate for phone giant Telmex to $3.35 from $3.76 per ADR, though it reiterated its outperform rating on the stock.
